retitle.title: NHS: prescription weight and diabetes medicines (GLP-1)

questions.text: You are planning a pregnancy after your cousin’s wedding. A forward says GLP-1 medicines are safe for everyone. What is the sensible move?
options: Start now and sort out the rest later
Tell a doctor about your plans before any decision
Wait for a friend who tried it to confirm
questions.explanation: Safety depends on the person. Pregnancy plans, health history and other medicines all matter, and these medicines are not used in pregnancy. A doctor weighs this before anything is prescribed.
questions.claim: Weight-management medicines are not for everyone and are not used in pregnancy or when planning one; a doctor decides after an individual review.

questions.text: An Instagram seller offers a cheaper pen with no prescription needed. What is the safer call?
options: Ask the seller which dose to start with
Buy it if the reviews look good
Use only what your doctor prescribes, from a registered pharmacy
questions.explanation: Some websites sell fake weight-loss medicines. Prescription medicines should come from a registered pharmacy, on a prescription from your own doctor, with follow-up.
questions.claim: Some websites sell fake weight-loss medicines; prescription medicines should be bought from a registered or approved pharmacy as directed by a health professional.

questions.text: It is a heavy, fried paratha day in the office tiffin and you feel queasy while on treatment. What often feels easier?
options: Skipping lunch to avoid feeling sick
Smaller, lighter meals through the day
A bigger dinner to make up for it
questions.explanation: Smaller, plainer meals more often tend to sit better, while fatty foods can make nausea worse. If you cannot keep fluids down, contact your care team.
questions.claim: Eating small meals more often and avoiding fatty foods can help with nausea; being unable to keep down fluids needs the care team.

questions.text: After a long commute with little water, you feel constipated on treatment. What can help?
options: Water, dal or sabzi for fibre, and a short walk
Cutting out all fibre
Borrowing a friend’s tablets
questions.explanation: Slower digestion and eating less can cause constipation. Fluids, fibre from dal, sabzi and fruit, and a short walk can help. If it does not settle, tell your care team.
questions.claim: Constipation is a common effect; fluids, fibre from lentils, vegetables and fruit, and movement can help, and persistent symptoms should go to the care team.

questions.text: Myth or fact: muscle is lost only with weight-loss medicines, never with plain dieting.
options: Myth
Fact
questions.explanation: Myth. Some muscle can be lost with any significant weight loss, including through diet alone. Strength training and enough protein help limit it.
questions.claim: The share of weight lost as lean mass is broadly comparable between incretin-based therapy and lifestyle weight loss; resistance training and protein help preserve muscle.

questions.text: Poha or idli for breakfast leaves you hungry by 11 am. Which addition brings in protein?
options: A second cup of sweet chai
Extra coconut chutney
Curd, sprouts or an egg on the side
questions.explanation: Protein foods such as eggs, curd, dal and sprouts help you feel full and help protect muscle during weight loss. A dietitian can adapt choices to your diet.
questions.claim: Protein helps build and maintain muscle and helps you feel full; eggs, lentils, beans and dairy are protein foods.

questions.text: You walk every morning and love it. What else helps protect muscle?
options: Walking a longer route is the only thing that matters
Strength exercise on two or more days a week
questions.explanation: Walking is great, and adults also need muscle-strengthening activity on 2 or more days a week. Squats, resistance bands or gym weights all count.
questions.claim: Adults need muscle-strengthening activity on at least 2 days a week in addition to aerobic activity.

questions.text: The weighing scale shows a drop. What does a body-composition scan such as DEXA add?
options: It tells you which medicine to take
It shows how much of the change is fat and how much is lean mass
It replaces a doctor’s advice
questions.explanation: The scale shows total weight only. A body-composition scan separates fat from lean mass, so a care team can see what is changing. It supports a doctor’s judgement, not replaces it.
questions.claim: Weight loss includes fat mass and fat-free mass; body-composition measurement shows the split, which total weight cannot.

questions.text: Diwali and wedding season knocked your routine off track. “I will restart next Monday” is the plan. What helps long term?
options: Treat it as failure and give up
Plan for festivals and keep follow-ups going
Wait for the perfect month to restart
questions.explanation: Weight management is long-term, and festivals and travel are normal life. A good plan expects them and keeps habits and follow-ups going instead of waiting for a perfect restart.
questions.claim: Obesity is a chronic condition; healthy eating and activity habits and follow-up continue over the long term.

questions.text: Myth or fact: in trials, many people regained a good part of their lost weight after stopping a weekly GLP-1 medicine.
options: Fact
Myth
questions.explanation: Fact. In one trial extension, participants regained a good part of their lost weight within a year of stopping. A plan for after, with habits and follow-up, matters.
questions.claim: In the STEP 1 extension participants regained about two-thirds of their prior weight loss a year after withdrawal; NIDDK says some regain is probable after stopping.

questions.text: Diabetes runs in your family and you carry weight around your belly, yet your BMI reads “normal”. What is the smart read?
options: A normal BMI rules out any risk
Belly fat can signal metabolic risk even at a normal-looking BMI, so ask a doctor about tests
Belly fat matters only for people who already have diabetes
questions.explanation: Indian consensus guidance notes more belly fat and metabolic risk at lower BMI levels than global charts assume. A doctor looks at waist, tests and family history, not BMI alone.
questions.claim: Asian Indians show more abdominal adiposity and the limits of normal BMI are narrower and lower than in white Caucasians.

questions.text: A health-camp sugar test came back normal. What else would a doctor want to look at?
options: Nothing, one sugar reading is the whole picture
Blood pressure, blood fats, sleep and family history
questions.explanation: Weight-related conditions include high blood pressure, abnormal blood fats and sleep apnoea as well as diabetes. A doctor looks at the full picture, not one sugar report.
questions.claim: Weight-related health problems include high blood pressure, dyslipidaemia, sleep apnoea, cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes; health professionals assess individual risk.

questions.text: You take tablets for diabetes. A reel says GLP-1 medicines can replace them. What should you do?
options: Halve your tablets to be safe
Stop your tablets and try it
Keep taking them and ask your own doctor before any change
questions.explanation: Never change diabetes medicines because of something you saw online. Some combinations need dose changes and monitoring, and stopping suddenly can affect blood sugar. Your own doctor decides.
questions.claim: Diabetes medicines and insulin may need adjustment alongside a GLP-1 medicine and treatment should not be stopped suddenly without talking to a doctor.

questions.text: Your uncle uses a GLP-1 injection for his diabetes. Is his pen and plan automatically right for you?
options: No. Uses and products differ, and a doctor decides what fits you
Yes, they are all the same
questions.explanation: GLP-1 medicines are used for diabetes, for weight management or for both, depending on the product. One person’s prescription is not a plan for someone else.
questions.claim: GLP-1 medicines can be used to manage type 2 diabetes or treat obesity depending on the product, and should be prescribed only after individual assessment.

questions.text: Myth or fact: someone who looks slim cannot have metabolic risk.
options: Fact
Myth
questions.explanation: Myth. Many Indians carry extra fat around the belly and organs even at a modest BMI, which raises metabolic risk. Looks are not a reliable guide; tests are.
questions.claim: Asian Indians exhibit excess body fat, abdominal adiposity and fat deposition in ectopic sites such as liver and muscle, driving metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes.

questions.text: Does one BMI number alone decide whether medicine is right for you?
options: Yes, the number settles it
No. BMI is one input, and doctors also weigh waist, tests and health conditions
questions.explanation: BMI is only one input. Guidance sets lower thresholds for people of South Asian background, and doctors also consider waist, health conditions and tests.
questions.claim: Eligibility uses BMI together with weight-related health problems, with lower BMI thresholds for South Asian backgrounds.

questions.text: A clinic asks for blood tests and a body-composition check before any plan. Why?
options: So decisions start from your own data, not a forwarded rule
To give everyone the same plan
To tick a formality before the real advice
questions.explanation: Choosing a treatment depends on your current health issues, other medicines and family history. Tests give a doctor your own data to decide with.
questions.claim: Medication choice depends on current health issues, other medicines and family medical history, which a health professional assesses.

questions.text: You are breastfeeding and a neighbour shares her weight plan. What should you do?
options: Follow it, since it worked for her
Speak to a doctor first, as these medicines are not recommended while breastfeeding
Take half of her dose
questions.explanation: Weight-loss medicines are not recommended while breastfeeding or pregnant. A doctor can suggest what is suitable for you instead.
questions.claim: Weight-loss medications are not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

questions.text: Your doctor says medicine is not the right step for you right now. What does that mean?
options: Nothing else will work
Find another seller
Food, movement and behavioural support can still help
questions.explanation: “Not now” is a valid answer. Healthy eating, activity and behavioural support still help, and your care team can revisit the plan as your situation changes.
questions.claim: Medicines are not for everyone with a high BMI; lifestyle programmes remain central and comprehensive care includes diet and activity.
